                "description": "* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected due to the combination\nof high tides and elevated surf.\n\n* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County\nCoastal Areas.\n\n* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Wednesday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding and minor coastal erosion\nexpected during high tides. Additionally, elevated surf will\nlead to strong rip currents.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 2-4 feet with local sets\nto 5 feet on south-facing beaches. These tide\npredictions have been corrected to reflect current trends in\nobserved tide observations.",

                "headline": "Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 28 at 9:16PM PDT until October 1 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA",
                "description": "* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is\npossible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal\nwaterways.\n\n* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San\nPablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.\n\n* WHEN...Now through 5 PM PDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only\nisolated road closures expected. High tides will result in\nflooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-\nlying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves\nfarther up the beach than typical.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide\nis expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.01 ft MLLW) at 1:30 PM\nTuesday 9/29, 1.2 ft above normal (7.03 ft MLLW) at 2:10 PM\nWednesday 9/30, and 1.1 ft above normal (6.92 ft MLLW) at 2:58\nPM Thursday 10/01. These predictions include up to 0.7 ft of\nsurge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding\nthreat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along\nthe Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,\nrespectively.",

For the Coastal Flood\nAdvisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the High\nSurf Advisory, breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with dangerous\nrip currents.\n\n* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County\nBeaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.\n\n* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Tuesday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some\nvulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time\nof high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,\nand harbor walkways. Moderate to locally significant beach\nerosion is likely. Very localized damage possible to most\nvulnerable areas. There is an increased risk for ocean\ndrowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to\nsea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off\nbeaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of most concern are Avalon, Long\nBeach (Peninsula and Belmont Shore). While the surf will\nlikely be smaller than Marie (from earlier this month), the\nlingering erosion effects enhance the vulnerabilities for\nlocally more significant coastal flooding.",
                "instruction": "Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do\nNOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.\n\nRemain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay\nnear occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in\nsuch conditions, stay off the rocks.\n\nRemain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or\nstay near occupied lifeguard towers.
